instructionText: Lead with the answer, then explain.
Start sentences with the actor doing the thing, then the verb.
Prefer plain Anglo-Saxon words to Latinate ones: "use" over "utilize", "start" over "initiate", "so" over "consequently", "because" over "insofar as".
Cut every phrase that does not change the meaning if removed.
source: run 2 — 6 tasks x 5 replicates, n=30. See LIB_RPT_qualifier-carveout_2026-08-02.md
rescoredAt: 0.3.0 — the HEDGE_IGNORE_DEFAULT and CLARITY_IGNORE_DEFAULT fixes changed directness and clarity scores, moving the composite from 83.6 to 89.4 and clarity from 54.1 to 90.7. No gated metric is affected: words, jargonPct, sentenceSimplicity and gradeBand are independent dimensions and are unchanged.

tolerances.note: Judgment calls, not derived from a variance estimate. They are set to catch a register change, not to detect small drifts. Widen them rather than chase noise.

words.rationale: 24% above baseline. The no-instruction control ran 550 on the 4-task set, so anything approaching that means the instruction stopped landing.

jargonPct.rationale: Control was 11.1 on the 4-task set. Crossing 10.5 means vocabulary is back at baseline.

sentenceSimplicity.rationale: Sits between E's observed range (69.2 run 2, 72.2 run 1) and E', which scored 60.3 and was called a style regression in the report. Gives E about 6 points of headroom and catches E' by about 3. A judgment call — the gate should agree with the report, which is why it is not set below 60.3.

gradeBand.rationale: Catches over-simplification. Variant C hit 57.6 by falling below the band floor.

knownGap: There is no no-instruction control on the 6-task set. Run 1's control (550 words, 11.1% jargon) used the 4-task set, so the deltas above mix task sets. Any re-run should include a control arm so the comparison is within-run.
